A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LEO research, despite the changed title and expanded scope. Text, figures, tables, and equations are readable. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2 includes a readable Appendix A.1–A.7.

before.justification: v1 reports original LEO benchmark results, autonomous-driving evaluation, training and fusion ablations, and qualitative examples in Tables 1–7 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains original LEO evaluations and adds experiments on encoder combinations, tiling, fusion, training-data scale, and computational efficiency, including appendix results.

M1.justification: The final LEO architecture retains InternViT-300M and SAM-L, dynamic tiling with global context, pixel unshuffling, independent MLP projectors, tile-level token interleaving, and InternLM2-7B. v2 formalizes and evaluates these existing components; its expanded experimental variants do not establish a redesign of the proposed model.

E1.justification: v2 adds MathVista evaluation for visually grounded mathematical reasoning. The original 13 general benchmarks remain represented in Appendix Table 13, and LingoQA remains included. Thus, the abstract's change from 13 to 11 benchmarks reflects the main comparison's scope, not removal of the original coverage.

E2.justification: v2 substantially revises the comparison sets: Table 4 adds DeepSeek-VL, SPHINX, MoME-X3, MouSi-X3, and Eagle-X3, while Table 7 introduces RADIO, RADIO2.5, and MoVE-KD-v1.1. Appendix Table 13 adds further general models. QwenVL, QwenVL-Chat, and Eagle-X4 comparisons disappear. MouSi-X2 matches the earlier Mousi comparator rather than constituting a new baseline.

E3.justification: v2 introduces controlled experiments varying tiling, encoder pairs, merging strategies, and fusion timing, with controls specified in Appendix A.2. It also adds Eagle-1.8M SFT variants, averages across eight benchmarks, and efficiency measurements, including a prescribed 1024-by-1024 image and generation prompt. These are new evaluation designs; the main LEO training recipe remains substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: The limited v1 ablations expand into systematic tests of four tiling strategies, four merging strategies, and pre/post-adaptation fusion across encoder pairs. v2 also adds training-data scaling, efficiency tradeoffs, and explicit failure cases in Appendix A.5–A.7. The original encoder-freezing and channel-fusion results are retained, but v1 Table 7's LingoQA tiling ablation is omitted.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for its experimental results. v2's added averages aggregate benchmark scores rather than repeated trials.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive fusion, tiling, efficiency, scaling, and qualitative results, including LEO's MathVista score of 37.2. The original 13 LEO benchmark scores and LingoQA scores are retained. Instruct-BLIP's VizWiz value changes from 45.5 in v1 Table 1 to 34.5 in v2 Table 13. The separate MMMU test score and LingoQA no-tiling results disappear.

T1.justification: v2 adds tensor notation, projector mappings, and the standard autoregressive factorization in Equation 1 to describe the existing procedure. These are explanatory formalizations, with no substantive new mathematical assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on a novel hybrid architecture and broad superiority over general and hybrid MLLMs. v2 makes a systematic empirical study of MoVE design principles the primary contribution, presenting LEO as their integration and emphasizing comparisons within MoVE. The earlier claim of being the first hybrid-MLLM exploration for autonomous driving is removed.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations for overlapping-tile redundancy, interleaving's spatial benefits, independent alignment, and freezing encoders to avoid catastrophic forgetting. It discusses accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs and limited benefits from additional SFT data. Beyond v1's tile-budget limitation, it adds fixed-encoder/7B constraints and analyzes failures involving road markings and document relationships.

D1.justification: Appendices A.1–A.2 substantially expand evaluation documentation, including benchmark subsets, the 1,000-example LingoQA evaluation, and staged experimental controls. Efficiency inputs and distilled-model resolutions are specified. The abstract changes a promised release to stated code availability. However, v1's explicit pixel-unshuffle factors and LingoQA Scenery/Action training-data instructions are omitted; these omissions do not establish changed settings.

R1.justification: v2 broadens related work to knowledge-distilled encoders and newer visual-understanding approaches, adding works such as RADIO, RADIOv2.5, MoVE-KD, and MoME. It repositions Eagle from a concurrent comparator to a preceding empirical study and explicitly frames LEO's fusion investigation as complementary. This changes research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around three investigative directions. A dedicated empirical-study section now precedes the LEO description. General-model comparisons and detailed ablations move into a new multipart appendix, substantially changing the narrative and document organization.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a single-column journal layout, redraws the overview and fusion diagrams, and reorganizes comparison tables. Main-text averages are paired with full appendix tables, and new efficiency and success/failure displays are added. The original tiling illustration and qualitative montage are retained under new figure numbers rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central fusion-design claims. Where v1 relied heavily on comparisons between different published models and limited ablations, v2 directly compares fusion timing and merging choices across multiple encoder pairs. Efficiency measurements and concrete failure cases also make benefits and boundaries clearer. The omitted driving-tiling ablation and some lost implementation details are drawbacks, and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but the stronger controlled evidence provides a substantial net improvement in paper quality.
